1.why: All /api/mfa* handlers derive the MFA record from session.accountId via recordFor(session.accountId), never from a client-supplied identifier, so settings always belong to the signed-in user.

2.why: Identity codes are bound to a specific pre-auth cookie/account (pending.identityCode compared with timingSafeEqual) and TOTP/recovery codes are per-account secrets, so a code cannot work for another user.

3.why: There is no session invalidation or rotation when MFA is enabled in /api/mfa/confirm, so pre-existing sessions in the sessions map remain valid (only idle/absolute timeouts apply).

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored AES-GCM encrypted via encryptSecret and recovery codes are stored only as HMAC-SHA256 (peppered) hashes in record.recoveryCodes.

5.why: randomToken, secureSixDigitCode, secureSecret, and secureRecoveryCode all use crypto.getRandomValues, and AES key generation uses crypto.subtle.generateKey.

6.why: Session and pre-auth tokens are HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict __Host- cookies and nothing is written to localStorage; however the CSRF token and the enrolment secret live in JS memory and in TEST_MODE mock codes/recovery codes are printed to the console and logs panel.

7.why: Server-side validators validEmail, validPhone, validOtp, and normaliseRecovery strictly regex-check all inputs, and apiBody rejects non-object JSON; no SQL is used (in-memory Maps).

8.why: Dynamic values (secret, provisioning URI, recovery codes, status text) are inserted via textContent/createElement; innerHTML is used only with static developer-authored strings, and a nonce-based CSP without unsafe-inline further mitigates XSS.

9.why: The application performs no redirects at all, so there is no redirect allow-list implemented (vacuously safe but the statement is not literally true of the code).

10.why: securityHeaders sets a strict nonce-based CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', HSTS max-age=31536000, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and X-Frame-Options: DENY on every response.

11.why: secureCookie/expiredCookie always emit HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict with the __Host- prefix and Path=/.

12.why: Errors are generic with no stack traces and secrets are only delivered in POST response bodies (never URLs), but in TEST_MODE the mock identity code is returned in the JSON response and recovery codes are logged to the console and visible Logs panel.

13.why: Identity codes expire after PREAUTH_TIMEOUT_MS and are marked used/deleted; TOTP counters are recorded in usedSetupCounters to prevent reuse; recovery codes are flagged true once consumed.

14.why: failAttempt with MAX_FAILURES=5 and LOCK_MS=10 minutes locks identity verification, MFA confirmation, and recovery-code use, returning 429 when locked.

15.why: A fresh session token is issued at identity verification (pre-auth cookie expired), idle (15 min) and absolute (8 h) timeouts are enforced in authenticated(), and logout deletes the session and clears the cookie — but no rotation occurs on the later MFA step-up.
